### Question 1.

Install the packages `shiny` and `rsconnect`, and update RStudio to version 2026.04 or later (Help -> Check for Updates). Older versions of RStudio cannot publish to Posit Connect Cloud.

In this question, you will build and publish your first shiny app on [Posit Connect Cloud](https://connect.posit.cloud). Follow these steps:

1. Create a new R Script (File -> New R Script). 

2. Copy [these code](c1.R) to the file. 

3. Save the file as `app.R` in a newly created folder. 

4. Press `Ctrl + Shift + Enter` to run the app locally. 

5. Go to https://connect.posit.cloud and create a free account. Signing up with your GitHub account is the easiest choice.

6. Go back to the app (if you closed it, hit `Ctrl + Shift + Enter` to reopen it) and click `Publish` (the blue icon) on the top right corner. 

7. Choose **Posit Connect Cloud** as the destination, sign in when asked, and follow the instructions to publish the app on the Internet. 

8. When publishing finishes, the app opens in your browser. Copy its link; this is the link you submit.

**Alternative: publish from GitHub.** If the Publish button does not work for you, you can publish from a public GitHub repository instead.

- Put `app.R` and any data file it reads in a folder of a **public** GitHub repository. 

- In R, set that folder as the working directory and run the code below. It creates a `manifest.json` file that tells Connect Cloud which version of R and which packages your app needs.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
rsconnect::writeManifest()
```

- Commit and push `app.R`, the data file, and `manifest.json` to GitHub. 

- On https://connect.posit.cloud click `Publish`, choose **Shiny**, then pick your repository, the branch, and `app.R` as the primary file. 

- If you later add or update packages, run `rsconnect::writeManifest()` again and push the new `manifest.json`.

### Question 2 - selectInput

Write a shiny app that can plot barplot of two categorical variables in the titanic dataset, [Example of the barplot](https://bryantstats.github.io/math421/slides/6_viz.html#39).

[Similar Apps](https://fa20.shinyapps.io/selectinput/) and [Codes](shiny_fa21/selectinput/a2.R)

Notice:  

- Two different shiny apps should be in two different folders. 

- You should not use local path when reading a data file.  For example,  do not use `read_csv('C://final//titanic.csv')`.  Instead, create a new folder and put the data file (titanic.csv) and the code file in the folder just created and use `read_csv('titanic.csv')`

### Question 4 - sliderInput

Write a shiny app that creates a plot for the adult census dataset.  The user inputs two variables and can change the range of `Age` (i.e., use `sliderInput`). 

[Similar Apps](https://sonfed.shinyapps.io/sliderInput/) and [Codes](shiny_fa21/sliderInput/a2_1.R)

-------

Notice:  Every app you publish counts toward the limits of your Posit Connect Cloud free plan. Check your plan's limits at https://connect.posit.cloud, and delete test apps you no longer need. 

You could also embed several shiny apps in one Rmarkdown and publish that document as a single app.  Do the following to embed a shiny app in an Rmarkdown. 

- Create an Rmarkdown

- Insert a code cell (`Ctrl + Alt + I`)

- Copy the codes of the shiny to the code cell

- Knit it 

- When asked, choose `Yes, Always.`

- Here is an example: https://fa20.shinyapps.io/a9_markdown/
